usage: agentless-mcp-server [-h] [--version] [--root DIR] [--roots-from FILE]
                            [--allow-client-roots] [--no-auto-warm]
                            [--no-auto-index] [--no-auto-restart]
                            [--surface {v1,v2,both}]
                            [--transport {stdio,http}] [--host ADDR]
                            [--port N] [--max-concurrency N]
                            [--call-limit SECONDS] [--recache-grace SECONDS]

Read-only MCP server over the agentless-mcp read surface.

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --version             show program's version number and exit
  --root DIR            a repository this server may serve; must exist at
                        startup; repeatable
  --roots-from FILE     a file of repository paths, one per line, added to
                        --root; blank lines and #-comment lines are skipped
                        and relative paths resolve against the working
                        directory, as --root does; repeatable
  --allow-client-roots  let the connected client's advertised MCP roots
                        authorise repositories, not merely select among --root
                        directories. This hands the client the operator's
                        decision about what is servable
  --no-auto-warm        do not warm cold grammars in the background at
                        startup; grammars then warm only through agentless-mcp
                        warmup (AGENTLESS_MCP_NO_AUTO_WARM in the environment
                        does the same)
  --no-auto-index       do not refresh a stale tag cache in the background
                        when a repository is first served; the cache then
                        updates only through agentless-mcp index
                        (AGENTLESS_MCP_NO_AUTO_INDEX in the environment does
                        the same)
  --no-auto-restart     do not restart the HTTP server when its installed
                        package changes; the process then serves the code it
                        loaded at startup until restarted by hand
                        (AGENTLESS_MCP_NO_AUTO_RESTART in the environment does
                        the same)
  --surface {v1,v2,both}
                        which tool surface to publish: v2, the six
                        consolidated intent-shaped tools, is the only one. v1
                        and both were removed in 0.11.0 and are refused at
                        startup
  --transport {stdio,http}
                        how the server talks to its client: stdio (the
                        default) for a client that launches this process, http
                        for one long-lived server several clients share over
                        the streamable-http transport
  --host ADDR           address --transport http binds; loopback only, default
                        127.0.0.1
  --port N              port --transport http binds; 1-65535, default 8000
  --max-concurrency N   how many tool handlers may hold worker threads at
                        once; 1-64, default 8. Raise it for a --transport http
                        server several clients share
  --call-limit SECONDS  how long one tool call may work before it stops with a
                        refusal; a call the client cancels also stops. Default
                        30
  --recache-grace SECONDS
                        extra time a call may spend parsing files the tag
                        cache does not hold, on top of --call-limit. Default
                        60

agentless-mcp-server: error: --allow-client-roots cannot be combined with --transport http. That flag lets the connected client's advertised roots authorise repositories, which is safe under stdio because the client is the process that spawned this server. Over HTTP the client is whatever reaches the port, and loopback is not per-user isolated, so any local process could name its own root and read anything this server's user can read -- the --root allowlist would stop deciding what is servable. Drop --allow-client-roots and enrol the repositories with --root or --roots-from.

options:

  --allow-client-roots  let the connected client's advertised MCP roots
                        authorise repositories, not merely select among --root

                        decision about what is servable
  --no-auto-warm        do not warm cold grammars in the background at

  --no-auto-index       do not refresh a stale tag cache in the background
                        when a repository is first served; the cache then

                        (AGENTLESS_MCP_NO_AUTO_INDEX in the environment does
                        the same)
  --no-auto-restart     do not restart the HTTP server when its installed
                        package changes; the process then serves the code it
                        loaded at startup until restarted by hand
                        (AGENTLESS_MCP_NO_AUTO_RESTART in the environment does
                        the same)
  --surface {v1,v2,both}

                        consolidated intent-shaped tools, is the only one. v1

  --transport {stdio,http}

                        the streamable-http transport
  --host ADDR           address --transport http binds; loopback only, default
                        127.0.0.1
  --port N              port --transport http binds; 1-65535, default 8000
  --max-concurrency N   how many tool handlers may hold worker threads at
                        once; 1-64, default 8. Raise it for a --transport http
                        server several clients share
  --call-limit SECONDS  how long one tool call may work before it stops with a
                        refusal; a call the client cancels also stops. Default
                        30
  --recache-grace SECONDS
                        extra time a call may spend parsing files the tag
                        cache does not hold, on top of --call-limit. Default
                        60
